scope: Corollary 10.3 (Weak-L1 maximal bound) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 075 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9a77d41e5b9b9beb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 75. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On T = R/(2πZ) with dµ = dx/(2π), set Φ(t) = t log(2 + t) and define the Luxemburg norm by ∥f∥Φ = inf {︃ b > 0 : ∫︂ T Φ(|f|/b) dµ ≤ 1 }︃ . For the ordinary symmetric partial sums of Theorem 1.1, put S∗f = supN≥0 |SN f|. There is an absolute constant C such that sup λ>0 λ µ{S∗ f > λ} ≤ C∥f∥Φ (f ∈ L log L(T; C)). (10.11)
